question: What claim is made about the yoginī named by wish with respect to who states her and by what means?
premises: A yoginī named by wish is posited.
She is stated by the siddhas up to Māyā.
This is done by supreme will.
inference: The yoginī named by wish is presented as having been stated by the siddhas up to the end of Māyā, by supreme will.
uncertainties: The exact force of 'up to Māyā' is not determinable from this verse alone.
plain_english: The yoginī named by wish was stated by the siddhas up to Māyā, by supreme will.
